investigation.title: Remote Agent Creation Blocked by Swarm Agent Quota Limit (409 Conflict)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-16T20:55:50–54Z with an identical 409 Conflict response from POST /api/agents, carrying the message "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". Because the agent creation call is the first step in every remote-agents check, the quota rejection prevented any evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) from being collected, causing all three checks to fail with empty evidence objects.
investigation.rootCause: The production swarm backend rejected POST /api/agents with HTTP 409 and error code "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". The eval probe account's organization has reached the 100-agent hard limit enforced by the swarm service. Because createAgent() is called at the very start of each remote-agents check (run-status-probes.mjs line 1339), the quota rejection is the single upstream failure that cascades into all three sibling check failures and leaves all required evidence fields unpopulated. This is an eval infrastructure failure against the production API; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Creation Blocked by Swarm Agent Quota Limit (409 Conflict)
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-16T20:55:50–54Z with an identical 409 Conflict response from POST /api/agents, carrying the message "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". Because the agent creation call is the first step in every remote-agents check, the quota rejection prevented any evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) from being collected, causing all three checks to fail with empty evidence objects.
investigations.rootCause: The production swarm backend rejected POST /api/agents with HTTP 409 and error code "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". The eval probe account's organization has reached the 100-agent hard limit enforced by the swarm service. Because createAgent() is called at the very start of each remote-agents check (run-status-probes.mjs line 1339), the quota rejection is the single upstream failure that cascades into all three sibling check failures and leaves all required evidence fields unpopulated. This is an eval infrastructure failure against the production API; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Image Generation Stream Eval Failure: SESSION_OPEN_FAILED (404) on production-api Runtime — Agent Harness Unreachable
investigations.summary: The image-generation-stream eval for the production-api runtime environment failed immediately (latencyMs=2050) with a SESSION_OPEN_FAILED error carrying a 404 response, indicating the agent runtime harness endpoint targeted by the eval runner is unreachable or misconfigured. The identical check passed on the desktop-release runtime (latencyMs=133754, imageUrlPresent=true, generation_completed frame present), confirming the image generation capability itself is functional and the failure is isolated to the production-api harness endpoint resolution.
investigations.rootCause: The eval runner called /api/generate/image/stream against the production-api runtime environment and received a 404 before any generation work could begin, surfaced as a generation_error frame with code SESSION_OPEN_FAILED. The harness endpoint resolved by SWARM_BASE_URL or LOCAL_HARNESS_URL for the production-api target is either not deployed, deployed at a different path or version, or the environment variable pointing to it is misconfigured for this runtime environment. This is an eval infrastructure / harness connectivity failure scoped to the production-api runtime; it is not evidence of a user-facing image generation outage, as the desktop-release sibling check passed concurrently.

The production-api harness is running an incompatible version that no longer exposes the /api/generate/image/stream endpoint at the expected path, causing a 404 on the route.

The production-api runtime environment requires a different authentication or routing configuration than desktop-release, and the eval runner's args (token, base URL) are not correctly set for this target, causing the request to hit an unmatched route.
